text: Inference (anumana) is the production of inferential knowledge (anumiti). Inferential knowledge is knowledge arising from a reason (paramarsha). A reason is knowledge of the pervaded-pervader relationship (vyapti) and the property of the subject (paksha-dharmata). For example, the knowledge “This mountain is smoke-bearing, and smoke is pervaded by fire” is a reason. The knowledge arising from this, “The mountain is fire-bearing,” is inferential knowledge. The universal concomitance (vyapti) is the regular association that wherever there is smoke, there is fire. The property of the subject (paksha-dharmata) is the presence of the pervaded (smoke) in the mountain and so on. ||40||
